A.summary: Evil is not a mere privation, because evil comes in degrees and privation does not.

B.summary: Privation can come in degrees, so evil can be a privation: more evil means farther from the good.

c1.text: Privation does not admit of more or less, because 'lacking' and 'not lacking' are contradictory and allow no middle ground.

c2.text: Existence admits of more or less, since there are degrees of perfection in existence.

c3.text: Among evil things, some are more evil than others.

c4.text: Evil is not a mere privation.

c5.text: Privative concepts such as inequality, dissimilarity and darkness admit of more or less.

c6.text: A privation can increase or decrease according to the increase or decrease of its cause.

c7.text: Evil is a privation: something is more evil when it is farther removed from the good.

c8.text: A privation is a partial negation of existence, so it depends on the existence it lacks.

c9.text: Good can exist without evil, but evil cannot exist without good.

c10.text: Evil is a kind of existence, ontologically on a par with good.

c11.text: Evil can exist independently of good.

a.note: Unlike A, B argues that evil is a privation.

b.note: A acknowledges degrees of evil and B agrees.

c.note: Better supported by B than by A: B can derive it, A cannot. Needs c8 from the rationale.
